summary: The core is built from the shared Capcom (GnG-family) video blocks: a DMA engine that takes the Z80 bus with BUSRQ/BUSAK, a per-line sprite search into a small object buffer, a draw stage paced by an object/pixel counter chain, and ping-pong line buffers. Tile and character layers are fetched pixel by pixel, with fetch phases decoded from H counter bits. None of this mirrors MAME's draw_sprites/screen_update/tile_info structure, and timing comes from raster counters (V[5] sound IRQ, V[7:5]-gated main IRQ), not from MAME's vblank and periodic interrupt callbacks. The top-level video mixer (jt1943_video) and the priority PROM logic are not in the listed files, so I did not review them.

findings.signal: sprite DMA via Z80 bus request
findings.note: Writing C806 (OKOUT) starts a state machine that raises bus_req, waits for the Z80's busak_n and for vblank, then counts full_cnt to copy OBJMAX bytes while blcnten switches the work RAM's address mux to obj_AB. MAME just does a buffered-spriteram memcpy.

findings.signal: per-line sprite search and object buffer
findings.note: Each scanline, a SEARCH/TRANSFER machine scans the DMA copy, compares Y against VF with an adder (Vsum, MATCH = &Vsum[7:4]) and copies up to OBJMAX_LINE matching 4-byte entries into a double-buffered line object RAM. MAME's draw_sprites instead loops over the whole sprite RAM once per frame, from offs = bytes-32 down to 0 with a 32-byte stride.

One counter {over, objcnt, pxlcnt}, preloaded with 32-OBJMAX_LINE at HINIT, sequences the draw. Each pxlcnt value latches a different attribute byte (ID, attr, Y, X), and the low pxlcnt bits form the ROM address, which works like a 74161 chain with load.

findings.signal: adder expressions instead of MAME arithmetic
findings.mame_ref: gunsmoke.cpp:draw_sprites (sx = spriteram[3] - ((attr&0x20)<<3); sy = 240 - sy on flip)
findings.note: The vertical match is (~VF + {~flip..,1}) + objY, a two's-complement sum with flip folded into the carry-in. Horizontal position is the 9-bit {hover, X} replacing MAME's subtraction and its 240-sx flip arithmetic. Off-zone objects are pushed to XOUT, not skipped.

findings.signal: ping-pong line buffers driven by the pixel clock
findings.note: Two line RAMs swap roles on each line: one is written at flip^posx with a transparency test, the other is read by an Hcnt reset during LHBL and erased after read (weA/weB = LHBL && st[0]). This is a scan-time pipeline, not a frame-bitmap blit.

findings.signal: tile/char fetch phases from H counter bits
findings.note: Map RAM is read and the ROM address is latched when HS[2:0]==DATAREAD. Shift registers x/y/z are loaded at DATAREAD+1 and then shifted every pixel. H7 and Hsum are built from H/HF bits with flip XORs. This replaces MAME's tile_info callbacks and tilemap scroll objects.
One H counter runs 128..511 and V is clocked at H==511. LHBL and LVBL are set at fixed H/V counts, and LVBL_obj runs two lines ahead for the sprite buffers. MAME only gives the raw screen parameters.

findings.signal: interrupts from raster bits, not callbacks
findings.note: The main IRQ fires on the falling edge of LVBL && V[7:5]!=3, latches into int_n and clears on IORQ&M1 acknowledge. The sound CPU's interrupt is V[5] from the video counter. MAME uses irq0_line_hold on vblank and a separate periodic timer.

Chip selects come from a casez on A[15:13]/A[12:11]/A[2:0], so C000-C7FF mirrors the input ports through A[2:0]. The core has no counterpart to MAME's protection_r patch at C4C9, which suggests the decode follows the board's partial decoding.

The C804 bits (CHON=7, flip=6, sound reset=5, bank=3:2) and D806 bits (OBJON=5, SCRON=4, obj bank=2:0) match MAME's handlers. A correct core must share these. The core also drives the sound reset from bit 5, which MAME ignores.
Per-game LAYOUT case branches remap attribute bits across many Capcom boards. This is FPGA reuse engineering. It points neither to MAME nor to one specific schematic.
